qt: to the Commission Marcin Sypniewski (ESN) Subject:

Regulation (EU) 2025/40 on Packaging and Packaging Waste (PPWR) imposes a number of obligations on importers concerning, among other things, the verification of packaging compliance, technical documentation and declarations of conformity. For small businesses importing goods from outside the EU, particularly in the e-commerce sector, these obligations may cover hundreds or thousands of products and overlap with national record-keeping systems, such as Poland’s BDO. In light of the above: 1.

Has the Commission carried out an assessment of the actual administrative costs arising from the PPWR for micro, small and medium-sized importers, in particular businesses importing a large number of different products from outside the EU?
How does the Commission intend to prevent the duplication of registration, recordkeeping and reporting obligations arising from the PPWR and existing national systems, such as Poland’s BDO?

Is the Commission considering further simplifications, de minimis thresholds or simplified documentation and reporting standards for SMEs, in particular importers who have no real influence over the design of packaging by non-EU manufacturers?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (10.11.2026) The Commission`s impact assessment accompanying its proposal for the later Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation (PPWR)1 estimated the administrative costs on economic operators but did not generally differentiate between company size and business activity. However, it assessed in very specific areas the impact on smaller businesses and PPWR established mitigation measures for them, as appropriate. The Commission has proposed in the Environmental Omnibus proposal2 to suspend the obligation for EU producers to appoint an Authorised Representative (AR) when they conduct direct sale to end users in other Member States. This would immediately alleviate a significant burden for EU producers. In the Staff Working Document3 (SWD) for the Environmental Omnibus proposal, it was estimated that the average cost for a company to appoint an AR are at least several hundred euros. What PPWR already established is that manufacturers falling under the definition of micro-enterprises are waived from the requirement to issue the declaration of conformity. An Implementing Act under the PPWR, Article 44(14), will establish harmonised registration and reporting obligations, and once it is adopted Member States will have 18 months to establish national registers. Thereby duplicate reporting is avoided. In preparing the forthcoming Circular Economy Act, the Commission is examining more broadly how extended producer responsibilities schemes can be improved, with a focus on simplification, harmonisation and digitalisation, making full use of the Single Market.
1 Regulation (EU) 2025/40 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 19 December 2024 on packaging

and packaging waste, amending Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 and Directive (EU) 2019/904, and repealing Directive 94/62/EC, OJ L, 2025/40, 22.1.2025. 2 https://circulareconomy.europa.eu/platform/en/news-and-events/all-news/environmental-omnibus-has-beenpublished. 3 https://environment.ec.europa.eu/document/download/9cc9e1e8-13c4-45f3-b9bc90e7e1b8133e_en?filename=SWD_2025_990_1_EN_autre_document_travail_service_part1_v3.pdf.
